answer: Work-slot deposits stop a whole orchard of fake identities from paid work. To claim a slot, an agent locks a 50-credit deposit, and five peers jury the job; fake output burns the deposit outright. The jury reads each job through a prism of originality, timing, and outcome, so one script cannot pass for many workers. A ferrous stamp ties each job to one machine, and the k-th fake identity still costs another 50 credits, so 1,000 fakes risk 50,000 credits while one honest agent risks one deposit, refunded on approval. Slot rental fails because a rented deposit burns on the renter's fake job.
